sections.h2: Where is Concord, New Hampshire, and what does it cover?
sections.html:
Concord is the capital of New Hampshire and the seat of Merrimack County, in the south-central part of the state about 16 miles north of Manchester and 66 miles north of Boston. The city covers 67.2 square miles, of which 64 are land.

The Merrimack River runs northwest to southeast through the middle of the city. The Soucook River forms the eastern boundary with Pembroke, the Turkey River crosses the southwestern quarter, and the Contoocook River joins the Merrimack at Penacook. Penacook Lake, in the west, is the largest lake in the city and its main water source.

Property tax in Concord is a city, county and school matter, so the first thing to know is which part of the city your house is in. The villages are Penacook, Concord Heights, East Concord and West Concord, and downtown has its own North End and South End neighborhoods.

sections.h2: How does Concord's geography affect houses and taxes?
sections.html:
Downtown sits on a low terrace west of the river, while Concord Heights is a flat, sandy plain on top of a bluff about 100 feet above the Merrimack. Most of the city's commercial development since 1960 has been on the Heights. The highest point in the city is Oak Hill, at 860 feet.

Those landforms matter for a seller in practical ways.

  • Homes near the river and its tributaries should be checked against the FEMA flood map.
  • Penacook is served by the Merrimack Valley School District rather than the Concord School District, which can affect buyer interest and the school portion of the tax bill.
  • Older downtown and North End streets carry older construction, while the Heights is more recently developed.

Concord's climate is humid continental, with about 42 inches of precipitation, about 67.7 inches of snow, and roughly 15 nights a year below zero. Roofs, heating systems and insulation get tested every winter.

sections.h2: Why does Concord's role as state capital matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Concord has been the official seat of New Hampshire government since 1808, so state employment shapes housing demand. The State House, completed in 1819, is the oldest U.S. state capitol where the legislature still meets in its original chambers. Concord became the Merrimack County seat in 1823.

The city also hosts the New Hampshire State Prison, the state police and fire academies, NHTI, the University of New Hampshire School of Law and Concord Hospital, which opened in 1891 as Margaret Pillsbury General Hospital. Those institutions anchor steady rental and ownership demand near downtown, though a house sale still depends on the individual property.

sections.h2: When are Concord property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Concord bills twice a year and collects in four installments due July 1, October 1, January 2 and March 31. The July and October bills are estimates, each 25 percent of the prior year's total bill. The January and March payments are final and are adjusted for the earlier estimates.

The July and October bills are mailed together around June 1, and the January and March bills go out around December 1. Bills are based on the April 1 assessment under RSA 76:2. State law requires 8 percent interest on late balances, prorated daily, and the city cannot waive it.

sections.h2: What is the Concord property tax rate?
sections.html:
The state's 2025 rate table lists Concord at $29.11 per $1,000 of assessed value. That total is made up of $10.18 for the city, $2.54 for the county, $1.58 for the state education tax and $14.81 for the local school district. The rate was set on November 19, 2025, on a valuation of $4,967,453,081 and a total commitment of $154,257,720.

On a house assessed at $400,000, that rate would produce a bill of about $11,644 a year. That is an illustration of the arithmetic only, and your own assessment decides your bill.

The biggest share is the local school rate, and it is the piece that differs between the Concord School District and the Penacook area. If your house is in Penacook, confirm your exact rate with the city assessor.

Yes. Concord completed a citywide revaluation to bring assessments to full and true market value as of April 1, 2026. The New Hampshire Constitution requires values to be set anew at least once every five years, and the city's last revaluation was in 2021.

The city said new assessments would be announced in summer 2026 and finalized before the final 2026 tax bill in December 2026. Abatement applications are available in the Assessing office after December 1, 2026.

  • Compare your new assessment with recent sales of similar houses.
  • File an abatement application if you think the value is wrong.
  • If you are selling, expect a buyer to underwrite the new value rather than your old one.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Concord assessment?
sections.html:
You apply to the city for an abatement by March 1 following the notice of tax. Under RSA 76:16, a person aggrieved by an assessment who has complied with RSA 74 may apply in writing by March 1, and the city must grant or deny in writing by July 1. A failure to respond counts as denial. The city lists March 1, 2027 as the deadline for the current cycle.

If the city denies your request, the denial letter must explain the next appeal step. Owners can go to the Board of Tax and Land Appeals or to superior court, and the Board's number is 603-271-2578. The state sets the abatement form, so use the current one from the city or the Board.

sections.h2: What happens if Concord property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax can become a tax lien and, eventually, a tax deed, but the process takes at least two years. Under RSA 80:76, the collector executes a deed to the lienholder after 2 years from the execution of the lien if the land is not redeemed. At least 30 days before the deed, the collector must notify the owner under RSA 80:77 and mortgage holders under RSA 80:77-a, by certified mail.

The title company pays unpaid tax from your proceeds, so a sale while the lien is still redeemable resolves it. Because interest runs at 8 percent on late balances, waiting makes the payoff larger.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies when selling in Concord?
sections.html:
New Hampshire's real estate transfer tax is $0.75 per $100 of the price, and it is imposed on both buyer and seller. The tax is filed and paid online through Granite Tax Connect, and the Department of Revenue Administration call center is 603-230-5920.

On a $400,000 sale, the tax is $3,000 per party, shown as an example only. Who bears the cost in practice is set by your purchase and sale agreement, so read the closing costs line carefully.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Concord house fast?
sections.html:
A cash sale is the shortest path to closing, and a listing may fit a house in good condition. Concord's mix of state-government demand and older housing means houses vary a lot in condition. A cash buyer takes a house as-is, so a Concord property with deferred roof work, tenants or a tax balance can still sell.

  • Get a payoff statement from your lender and a balance from the Tax Collector.
  • Find your 2026 assessment and compare it with your old one.
  • Request a written offer and check who pays each closing cost.

We buy Concord houses as-is and do not charge commission or fees to the seller.

faqs.q: When are Concord property taxes due?
faqs.a: Concord's installments are due July 1, October 1, January 2 and March 31. July and October are estimates of 25 percent of the prior year's bill, and January and March are the final adjusted payments.

faqs.q: What is the Concord tax rate?
faqs.a: The state's 2025 rate table lists Concord at $29.11 per $1,000: $10.18 city, $2.54 county, $1.58 state education and $14.81 local school.

faqs.q: What is the interest on late Concord property tax?
faqs.a: The city says state law requires 8 percent interest, prorated daily, on balances past the due dates, and it cannot waive it.

faqs.q: What is the abatement deadline in Concord?
faqs.a: Under RSA 76:16, applications are due by March 1 after the notice of tax. The city lists March 1, 2027 for the current cycle, and forms are available in Assessing after December 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Concord house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax and interest are paid from the closing proceeds. A tax deed cannot be issued until at least 2 years after the lien is executed, with 30 days of notice before the deed.

faqs.q: Who pays the New Hampshire transfer tax?
faqs.a: The tax is $0.75 per $100 and is imposed on both buyer and seller. Your purchase agreement sets how the cost is divided in practice.
